schema.features: one entry per ufs-tells/1 feature id; the ids are stable, the numbers are not
schema.why: why the threshold sits where it does
schema.source: where the tell and, where it has one, the number come from (URL)
schema.note: the numbers are hand-set starting points. Fitted weights from human labels replace them here, with no code change (scripts/tells-render.mjs reads this file).

cream-ground.why: The largest-area opaque background among html, body, main and the first section, in OKLCH. L 0.90 and up is a paper ground; C 0.005 to 0.04 is tinted but not coloured (white is under 0.005); H 60 to 100 is the warm yellow-orange band. Bone (#f2efe7, oklch 0.952 0.011 91) and frontend-design's #F4F1EA both sit inside it.

perma-dark.why: The same ground at OKLCH L 0.25 or below, with no prefers-color-scheme: light rule anywhere in the page's readable stylesheets: dark with no way out.

cluster-1.why: frontend-design's first cluster: a cream ground, a serif display and a terracotta or clay accent (near #D97757, OKLCH H about 41). The accent is any colour a visible element renders in text, background or border at C 0.08 or more with H 20 to 60.

cluster-2.why: frontend-design's second cluster: near-black with one acid-green or vermilion accent. perma-dark, and the colours at C 0.15 or more fall in one hue group (hues within 30 degrees of a neighbour are one group).

template-chrome.why: frontend-design's fifth cluster, counted: text at 14 px or less set in uppercase with 0.08em or more of tracking; short labels (40 characters or fewer, pseudo-element counters included) in a monospace face; meta strings joined with ' · '; link and button text ending in an arrow. Four or more in all fires it: slop-detect's all_caps_labels needs two, and one tracked nav label plus one caption is not yet a kit.

overused-face.why: The first family named in the computed font-family of the first h1, the body and the first button is on SLOP_FONTS (scripts/audit.mjs), which since 2026-09-29 includes impeccable 4.1.0's Instrument Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans, Mona Sans, Open Sans and Geist Mono. The family the stack asks for, loaded or not: the tells run blocks every other origin, so a Google Fonts face never loads here, and it is the choice that is the tell. Whether it loaded is recorded beside it.

accent-word.why: A descendant of an h1 that differs from the rest of it in colour (OKLab distance over 0.03), in style (italic), in face, in weight (200 or more) or with gradient-clipped text, while the rest of the h1 still has text. frontend-design lists accenting a single headline word as a default.

decorative-numbering.why: Three or more siblings, each a heading or holding one, prefixed 01, 02, 03 in order: in the text, in a ::before string or a decimal-leading-zero counter, or as the list marker. Zero-padded only; a plain 1, 2, 3 in a real step list is not the tell.

stat-banner.why: Three or more siblings whose largest text is a number (12 characters or fewer, a unit or + allowed) set at twice the body size or more. slop-detect's stat_banner clusters three or more numerals at 28 px and up.

uniform-radius.why: Six or more boxes of at least 120 by 80 px sharing one non-zero border-radius and one box-shadow: frontend-design's SaaS card kit, one radius on everything and the same soft shadow under each.

marquee.why: A rule in the page's stylesheets that runs an infinite animation whose keyframes translate on x, a running infinite animation that does, or a <marquee>. The stylesheet counts even with no element using it: impeccable's CSS scan fires on the rule, and a chassis that ships the rule ships the device.

centred-share.why: The share of text blocks whose every line is centred within 2% of the viewport width of the page axis (and that are text-align: center, or shrink-wrapped so alignment cannot matter). Half or more, over at least five blocks, is a centred stack; slop-detect's centered_hero checks only the h1.

section-waterfall.why: The page's top-level blocks, each matched to the library section whose classes and ids it carries (IDF-weighted, 0.6 or more), run in exactly DEFAULT_SECTIONS: the scaffold's order, left as it came. The generic SaaS order is W5 and the audit's check.

display-tracking.why: Records the tightest letter-spacing on display text (28 px and up) in em. It fires at -0.05em or tighter, slop-detect's crushed_tracking line; the chassis's -0.02 to -0.035em does not. audit.mjs still warns when a stylesheet has no negative tracking at all, so the two disagree below -0.05 only in intent; which way the human labels lean decides it.
